report:
**Conclusion:** The health claim is **true**. Bystander hands-only (chest compression-only) CPR is strongly associated with significantly higher survival rates following an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) compared to receiving no bystander CPR.

### Evidence Summary

- **Increased Survival:** Large observational studies and registry data show that patients who receive immediate bystander CPR—including hands-only CPR—have roughly double to triple the likelihood of surviving to hospital discharge compared to those who receive no bystander CPR.
- **Comparable Effectiveness to Conventional CPR:** The American Heart Association (AHA) and resuscitation research demonstrate that hands-only CPR yields similar survival outcomes to conventional CPR (chest compressions combined with rescue breathing) in adult OHCA victims.
- **Reduced Delays to Care:** Hands-only CPR is simpler for laypersons to execute and can be rapidly guided by emergency dispatchers. Because hesitation is reduced, chest compressions begin sooner, maintaining critical brain and cardiac perfusion until professional paramedics arrive.

Overall, providing hands-only CPR offers a substantial survival benefit over taking no action during an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

### Sources

- **American Heart Association CPR Facts & Stats:** https://cpr.heart.org/en/resources/cpr-facts-and-stats/
- **JAMA Study on Layperson CPR and Survival:** https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/186668
- **AHA Science Advisory on Hands-Only CPR:** https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/circulationaha.107.189380
- **Swedish OHCA Registry Data Analysis:** https://medicalxpress.com/news/2019-04-compression-only-cpr-survival-out-of-hospital-cardiac.html
